purpose: Resolve each material citizen-facing claim to the appropriate official source, provision, record, version/date and retrieval route.
core_principle: CLAIM → AUTHORITY → EXACT SOURCE → VERSION/DATE → EVIDENCE OR PROVISION → OFFICIAL ROUTE
source_rules: Primary legal propositions should cite the applicable primary legislation or SI where available.
Case law supports only the proposition actually decided or reasoned in the relevant case.
Official guidance explains procedure or administration and must not be presented as legislation.
Property-specific facts require the relevant official property record or authorised official evidence route.
Current and historical claims require matching temporal source scope.
A source URL alone is not sufficient where the relevant provision, record or version must be identified.
If the official source is inaccessible or incomplete, the citation state must disclose that limitation.
property_route_examples: Land Register current folio/title plan → Tailte Éireann/LandDirect
Filed Land Registry document → Tailte Éireann Rule 159 route where access entitlement exists
Registry of Deeds search/memorial → Tailte Éireann Registry of Deeds services
Legal rule → Irish Statute Book or other authoritative legal source
hard_stops: Never cite a secondary source when an authoritative primary source is required and available.
Never cite a current consolidated source as proof of a historical version without temporal verification.
Never cite a general property page as proof of a property-specific fact.
Never invent a provision, record number, source date or retrieval route.
Never imply that a citation proves more than the cited source establishes.
